text:
Finance asked: "Why was order #8842 marked shipped before payment cleared?"

I opened the row. status = shipped. updated_at = Tuesday. That was the entire history — we'd overwritten every previous value.

CRUD stores what is true now. When you need what happened, you bolt on an audit table and hope it stays in sync. It usually doesn't.

Event sourcing flips it: append events (OrderCreated, PaymentAuthorized, OrderShipped). Current state is derived by replay. The log is the source of truth.

CQRS splits writes from reads — command side validates and appends; query side serves denormalized views. Read models lag a bit. That's normal.

Worth the complexity when audit, temporal queries, or many read shapes justify it. Overkill for a five-field admin form.

I wrote when to reach for this vs staying with CRUD + a real audit strategy.

https://blog.sandeepallala.com/blog/system-design-event-sourcing-and-cqrs
